title: Bug: benchmarks/run_suite.sh redirect sends results to wrong file
description:
## Finding

In benchmarks/run_suite.sh line 10:

    ./"$script" --agent "$AGENT" --dataset "$DATASET" $extra >out "$RESULTS_FILE" 2>&1

The ">out" redirects stdout to a literal file named "out". Then "$RESULTS_FILE" is passed as a positional argument to the script (not as a redirect). Finally 2>&1 redirects stderr to the same "out" file.

Result: Benchmark results are written to "out" instead of "suite_results.log".

## Fix

Change line 10 to:

    ./"$script" --agent "$AGENT" --dataset "$DATASET" $extra > "$RESULTS_FILE" 2>&1

This removes the stray "out" and properly redirects to "$RESULTS_FILE".

title: Inconsistency: error JSON format differs between read and edit commands
description:
## Finding

Error output format is inconsistent between read and edit commands.

**read command errors** (line 162 of src/main.rs):
    {"status":"error","detail":"failed","message":"..."}

**edit command errors** (line 224 of src/main.rs):
    {"status":"error","detail":"anchor_invalid","message":"..."}

The read command always uses detail="failed" (wrapped by main()), while edit uses specific detail codes (anchor_invalid, input_invalid, failed).

## Fix

Either:
1. Have read_command produce its own JSON error output (like edit_command does), or
2. Make edit_command use detail="failed" for generic errors

Option 1 is preferred for consistency with the existing edit error granularity. This means edit_command should NOT handle its own errors but let them propagate through run() -> main(). However, edit_command also needs to write the file and compute diffs on success, so a hybrid approach is best: have edit_command return a structured error type that main() formats consistently.

title: Dead code: _has_replace_all computed but never used in edit_command
description:
## Finding

In src/main.rs line 197:

    let _has_replace_all = edits.iter().any(|e| e.op == "replace_all");

This variable is prefixed with _ (unused) and never referenced. The replace_all check happens inside apply_edits_str() at lines 66-73.

## Fix

Remove line 197. The replace_all logic is already handled inside apply_edits_str().

title: Doc drift: apply_edits_str comment says "write back" but function returns string
description:
## Finding

In src/main.rs line 76:

    // Existing logic: read file, apply edits, write back

The function apply_edits_str returns a Result<String, EditError> — it does NOT write to disk. The write-back happens in edit_command (line 210).

## Fix

Change the comment to:

    // Existing logic: read file, apply edits, return content

Or remove the comment entirely since the function name and return type make the behavior clear.

title: Doc drift: SKILL_MARKDOWN omits diff field in edit success output
description:
## Finding

In src/main.rs SKILL_MARKDOWN (lines 109-137), edit success is documented as:

    success: {"status":"ok"}

But actual code (line 215-219) produces:

    {"status": "ok", "diff": diff}

The diff field is always included in success output but undocumented.

Also, the read command JSONL output format is not documented in SKILL_MARKDOWN.

## Fix

Update SKILL_MARKDOWN:
1. Change success format to: {"status":"ok","diff":"..."}
2. Add documentation for read command output format (already partially documented but could be clearer)
3. Document that edit error uses specific detail codes (anchor_invalid, input_invalid, failed)

title: Test gap: CLI commands (read_command, edit_command) and helpers (parse_edits, read_stdin, EditError) untested
description:
## Finding

The test modules in src/main.rs (tests, edit_write_tests, window_tests) cover:
- anchors_for / unique_anchor / four_char_hash
- payload_lines / split_file_lines
- window function
- fuzzy edit (via apply_edits_str)
- compute_diff / diff headers
- dry_run behavior

NOT tested:
- read_command: the entire CLI read path including error handling
- edit_command: the CLI edit path including success/error/JSON output
- parse_edits: parsing JSONL edit input, empty lines, malformed JSON
- read_stdin: reading from stdin
- EditError: all three constructors (anchor, input, failed)

## Fix

Add tests for:
1. parse_edits with valid JSONL, empty input, malformed JSON
2. read_command with valid path, missing file, --after/--offset mutual exclusion
3. edit_command error path (anchor not found) producing correct JSON
4. EditError constructors producing correct detail/message pairs

title: Type safety: serde_json::to_string(&line).unwrap() in production code (read_command)
description:
## Finding

In src/main.rs line 189:

    println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&line).unwrap());

The unwrap() in production code will panic if JSON serialization fails. While AnchoredLine only contains serializable types (String, usize), this is still a poor practice that masks failures.

## Fix

Replace unwrap() with expect() for a clearer panic message, or handle the error gracefully:

    println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&line).expect("AnchoredLine serialization should not fail"));

Or better, propagate the error through the Result chain.
